 Judgment
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

Varun Raj .R.P vs Venkatesh .T on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172249012/
1 2.
In the petition it is stated that on14.04.2021 at 3.00pm petitioner was pillion rider traveling on two wheeler bearing No.KA-41-AD-6329.When
he reached near Kunigal Circle NH- 75 Nelamangala- Bengaluru
, rider of the said motor cycle rode the said vehicle in high speed and in rash and negligent manner endangering human life.
When they approached road hump he suddenly applied brake.
As a result of which, accused rider and petitioner pillion rider fell down, due to which, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
He was shifted to Nelamangala Govt. hospital and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.

He was treated conservatively as fractures of left bracial plexus injury and he was discharged, but however the impact of accident aggravated and he was admitted to Kaveri hospital for further treatment and after operation internal implants were fixed and he was discharged on 18.08.2021.
He has incurred expenses to the tune of 6 lakhs towards medical treatment and other incidental charges.
3. He was aged 19 years hale and healthy at the time of accident.
He was working as Electrician and earning income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
He could not resume to his avocation till the filing of this petition.
The rider of aforesaid motor cycle was negligent.
The Nelamangala police have registered case in (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.3566/2021 Crime No. 240/2021 against the said rider.
1st respondent is R.C owner and 2nd respondent is insurance company holding valid insurance at the time of accident in respect of motor cycle.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 owner is served .
He remained absent on the date of hearing.
He is placed exparte.
Respondent 2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement.
He contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He admitted the insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-41-ED- 6329.
The same is valid from 07.06.2020 to 06.06.2021 and liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
1 st respondent not complied provisions of Sec.134(c) and police have not complied 158(c) of IMV Act.
The accident and involvement of accident is disputed.
The rider had no D.L and therefore owner is responsible to pay the compensation.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner is denied.
Manner of accident narrated by the petitioner is denied.
Treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses alleged by him are disputed.
Right reserved to contest the matter U/Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
That in case of compensation granted, interest cannot exceed Rs.6% p.a.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors- in-office has framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 14.04.2021 at about 3.00pm he was a pillion rider on Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-ED-6329 on Kunigal-Nelamangala NH-75 road and when he reached Kunigal Circle, the rider of the motor ycle rode the same at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly applied brake Varun Raj
.R.P vs Venkatesh

.T on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172249012/
2
seeing a road hump and caused accident, as a result of it, the pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation If yes, How much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6 . To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.19 documents are marked on his behalf.
M.R.O of Kaveri hospital, Electronic City, Bengaluru is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.20 and 21 documents are marked.
Dr. by name Nagaraj B.N is examined as P.W.3.
Through him Ex.P.22 and 23 documents are marked.
Staff of Nelamangala Govt. hospital is examined as PW.4.
Through her Ex.P.24 to 28 documents are marked.
On the contrary, I.O by name Anjan Kumar.V is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 to R.3 documents are marked.
Assistant Manager of 2nd respondent insurance company is examined as R.W.2.

Through him Ex.R.4 and 5 documents are marked.
(SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.3566/2021 7.
Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.

8. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Negative,
 Issue No.2: In the Negative,
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

As per the petition averments accident took place on 14.04.2021 at about 3.00 pm and petitioner was pillion rider on two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA-41-ED-6329.As per his cross examination the said vehicle belongs to his maternal uncle and h is maternal uncle's son was riding the two wheeler and this petitioner was sitting behind him as pillion rider.

Further as per the petition averments immediately after the accident petitioner was taken to Nelamangala Govt.
hospital first aid treatment was given, then he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru where X-ray was taken and fractures of left bracial plexus injury was found, but he was treated conservatively and discharged from Victoria hospital.

Further in the petition averments it is stated that after 4 months of the accident injuries were aggravated and he was admitted to Kaveri hospital,
Bengaluru.
As per the discharge summary produced by the petitioner, he was in Kaveri hospital as inpatient from 12.08.2021 to 15.08.2021.
In the said hospital, treatment of multiple nerve transfer left side was done.

As per the history mentioned in the discharge summary, petitioner complained of (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.3566/2021 immobility of right upper limb since 3 months and he had history of road traffic accident following which petitioner sustained injury to left upper limb 3 months ago.

Varun Raj .R.P vs Venkatesh .T on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172249012/
3

This goes to show that, complaint of the petitioner before the said hospital was immobility of right upper limb for which he has taken treatment, but he has given history of accident in which he sustained injury to left upper limb.

10. The first information is given by the petitioner himself as per the FIR registered by Nelamangala Traffic police on first information given by petitioner on 15.07.2021 i.e., after 3 months of the accident.

In the first information petitioner complainant informed that he sustained road traffic accident on 14.04.2021 in which his maternal uncle's son Chandrashekar was riding two wheeler KA-41-ED-6329 in which, this petitioner was sitting behind as pillion rider.
That when they reached near Kunigal circle, the rider did not observe humps and applied brakes suddenly by which the rider lost control and both of them fell on the road on the left side.
The vehicle sustained damages and both rider and pillion rider sustained injuries to their body.

11. That, Both of them were shifted to Nelamangala Govt. hospital and this petitioner has given his statement before police in the hospital in front of the doctor in which he stated to take action against the bike rider.
But, immediately thereafter his maternal uncle who is none other than R.C owner of the vehicle came to the hospital and stated that he will pay the medical expenses.
Believing his words this petitioner told (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.3566/2021 Nelamangala Police that case need not be registered.

Further he stated in the first information that on the same day, his maternal uncle took him to Victoria hospital in ambulance, but due to Covid-19 the doctors in that hospital did not admit him and told him to go to some other hospital.
Thereafter, the R.C owner got him treatment in different hospitals.

Thereafter this petitioner got MRI scan and found that 4 nerves are cut and operation has to be done, when this is informed to the R.C owner of the vehicle, the R.C owner told that he cannot give money for operation and he can proceed to give complaint if he wants.
Therefore, after 3 months of the accident first information is given.

12. On the basis of this information received by the Nelamangala Traffic police they registered Crime in FIR No.240/2021 against the rider of aforesaid two wheeler for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
It is necessary to notice that, though petitioner stated that he had grievous injury offence under section 337 of IPC is registered and not under section 338 of IPC.
On the same day of the first information spot panchanama is conducted in which the petitioner has shown the spot.

On 20.07.2021 vehicle inspection was done in which, fresh damages are found at head light assembly,
scratch guard left damaged, speedometer damaged, fuel tank both side damaged and the accident was not due to any mechanical defect.
Immediately after 13 days of the first information i.e., on 28.07.2021 final report is filed against the rider of the aforesaid two wheeler for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
On the (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.3566/2021 date of first information itself wound certificate is received by the Nelamangala Traffic police.
The same is produced at Ex.P.8.
It is issued by one Dr. Kantharaj in which, he mentioned history of fallen from bike as pillion rider after jumping from hump at 2.30 pm on 14.04.2021 near Kunigal Byepass.
Injuries found were abrasion about 2 X 2 cms over the anterior aspect of left knee, swelling and tenderness at superior aspect of left shoulder about 2 X 2 cms.

It is further mentioned in the wound certificate as under:
Further he himself had consulted Vinayaka Medical Center where he was found to be having left brachial plexus injury (on 19.04.2021) where he was further referred to Varun Raj .R.P vs Venkatesh .T on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172249012/
4 neurosurgeon.
Further he was examined by Dr.S.N.Narasimhamurthy, orthosurgeon at Punasru ortho centre, Bengaluru where he was diagnosis and treated for left 1st rib fracture with left brachial plexus injury.
13. Then he mentioned that, injury is grievous in nature.

This wound certificate issued by the doctor goes to show that, instead of mentioning what was the injury found when the patient was first seen by the doctor, it is mentioned about the further treatment taken by the patient after the alleged injury took place due to RTA on 14.04.2021.

The only two injuries mentioned by the doctor are abrasion on left knee,
swelling and tenderness of the left shoulder as per the Ex.P.8 wound certificate and Ex.P.25 MLC extract.
He has not mentioned which of those 2 injuries is grievous in nature, but he only mentioned that 'injury is grievous in nature.
As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary the complaint of the petitioner was immobility of right upper limb since 3 months.
But, as per the Ex.P.8 wound certificate tenderness was found on left shoulder, but there was no injury to right upper limb.
There is also no mention about injury to rib.

This creates doubt in the mind of court with respect to whether injury for which petitioner underwent operation was due to alleged RTA occurred on 14.04.2021.
15.

That apart, as per Ex.P.19 statement of petitioner before the Nelamangala Traffic police on 14.04.2021 on the same day when accident took place he stated that, he has given statement before the doctor to take action against rider of two wheeler Chandrashekar, but the said incident was accidental and Chandrashekar fell from the bike by loosing control by which accident took place,
therefore there is no need to take further action on the statement given before the doctor and he will not file complaint before the police.
This statement was recorded on the day of accident itself by the police.
16. P.W.1 has not stated actually he went to police station to give that statement on the day of accident itself.

On respondent side I.O is examined as R.W.1 and he stated that on 15.07.2021 request was given to Nelamangala Govt.hospital to furnish wound certificate, but in the requisition at Ex.R.1 it is mentioned as 14.07.2021.
On the same day wound certificate was given.
In fact he has received complaint on 15.07.2021 as per the FIR.

He has stated that he has not examined that for how many days petitioner took treatment at Nelamangala (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.3566/2021 hospital and not examined the documents of Victoria hospital where petitioner alleged to have taken treatment.
He has not submitted any requisition to Victoria hospital regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Varun Raj .R.P vs Venkatesh .T on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172249012/
5 17.

sentences.text: In the evidence of doctor P.W.3 he has mentioned that petitioner gave the history of RTA on 11.04.2021, but as per the FIR it is on 14.04.2021.
Therefore, whether there was any other accident occurred to petitioner other than the one mentioned in the petition is not explained.

Further, as per the evidence of doctor, petitioner was treated conservatively and discharged from Victoria hospital and there is no mention about any further treatment taken by petitioner in respect of alleged RTA,
though he claims that he has taken treatment at Cauvery hospital and he was operated.

As such,
history of medical treatment taken by the petitioner as explained by him before doctor does not tally with the treatment mentioned in the petition.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court, case of the petitioner does not inspire confidence to grant the relief claimed in the petition.
Further the delay in filing FIR is also not properly explained by the petitioner as the delay runs to more than 3 months from the date of accident.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court petitioner is not entitled for any compensation prayed in the above case.
Hence, I hold this Issue in the Negative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 : In view of the above reasons petitioner is not entitled for compensation in respect of alleged RTA dated 14.04.2021.
Hence, I answer this Issue in the Negative.
. ISSUE NO.3:-

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby dismissed with cost.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

Bangalore.
